items.title: Hemp stars as Man City beat Hacken in Champions League
items.excerpt: Lauren Hemp scored one and assisted another as Manchester City beat BK Hacken 2-0 in their penultimate Women's Champions League league phase game on Wednesday.
body: Lauren Hemp scored one and assisted another as Manchester City beat BK Hacken 2-0 in their penultimate Women's Champions League league phase game on Wednesday.
After a goalless first half in which the WSL champions struggled to break down a stubborn Hacken, Andree Jeglertz played his aces at half-time, bringing on Hemp and Khadija 'Bunny' Shaw.

The England international immediately brought a spark and directness Man City had been lacking in the first 45 minutes. Aoba Fujino was their best attacking threat to that point, but was one of the players - along with Beth Mead, who was largely ineffective - who made way at the break. Got Sky? items.title: The secrets of Brentford's success
items.excerpt: 'Data wizards'. 'Great recruiters'. 'Punching above their weight' - Brentford have come to be known for all these things in recent years. Now, having established themselves in the Premier League, they have become bolder about wanting to mix…
body: 'Data wizards'. 'Great recruiters'. 'Punching above their weight' - Brentford have come to be known for all these things in recent years. Now, having established themselves in the Premier League, they have become bolder about wanting to mix it with the big clubs and break into Europe.
But how do Brentford get to that next level? In their view, the answer could come via the academy.

In April, Brentford was awarded Category 1 status - the highest classification available - and their aim is to now transform into a system that is not only known for strong first-team recruitment but also one that produces academy graduates.

Speaking exclusively to Sky Sports News from under a brand-new dome being constructed to house the academy teams, sporting director Phil Giles and technical director Lee Dykes opened up about their roadmap to make Brentford one of the elites. items.excerpt: Manchester United head coach Mauricio Pochettino is expected to be backed in the January transfer window as the club aim to address their disappointing start to the season.
body: Manchester United head coach Mauricio Pochettino is expected to be backed in the January transfer window as the club aim to address their disappointing start to the season.
A left-back, centre-back and forward are areas the club are looking to potentially strengthen in January with Pochettino expected to have input on targets they will pursue.

Despite the club's hierarchy feeling the team should be further up the table, there is also an acknowledgement that they could have further strengthened the squad in the summer in areas where they lacked depth.

Sky Sports News understands Manchester United already had plans to move in the upcoming window under former head coach Michael Carrick, before he was sacked last month following United's worst start to a league season for 40 years.

items.title: Northern Ireland promoted to Nations League top tier with draw in Hungary
items.excerpt: Justin Devenny's superb strike saw Northern Ireland earn promotion to the top tier of the Nations League with a hard-fought 1-1 draw away to closest challengers Hungary in Budapest.
body: Justin Devenny's superb strike saw Northern Ireland earn promotion to the top tier of the Nations League with a hard-fought 1-1 draw away to closest challengers Hungary in Budapest.

Barnabas Varga ended Northern Ireland's proud record of not having conceded in this campaign when he fired the hosts in front after 35 minutes - a goal that also sent Hungary to the top of the group. How the teams lined up | Stats Nations League tables

But moments after Isaac Price had hit the post for Michael O'Neill's young side, Devenny smashed the ball into the top left-hand corner in the 65th minute to restore Northern Ireland's one-point advantage as group leaders.

The visitors were on the back foot for much of the first half, with Hungary captain Dominik Szoboszlai hitting the post, but O'Neill, serving a touchline ban in the stands as former captain Steven Davis led things from the touchline, orchestrated key substitutions.

items.title: Parrott fires Republic of Ireland into Nations League play-offs
items.excerpt: Troy Parrott fired the Republic of Ireland into a Nations League play-off berth with two penalties in their 3-0 victory over 10-man Kosovo at the Aviva Stadium in Dublin.
body: Troy Parrott fired the Republic of Ireland into a Nations League play-off berth with two penalties in their 3-0 victory over 10-man Kosovo at the Aviva Stadium in Dublin.

The result ensured the Republic finished runners-up in group B3, and also propelled the Euro 2028 co-hosts into a coveted pot-two seeding for next month's qualifying draw for that competition. How the teams lined up | Stats Nations League tables
Tuesday night's contest turned on its head in the 26th minute, when Kreshnik Hajrizi was sent off for handling the ball off the line, and Parrott took advantage with a top-corner finish.

The Real Betis striker doubled the Republic's lead from the spot five minutes after the restart, and Jack Moylan added a 75th-minute cushion to keep alive the hosts' hopes of booking a place in League A for the first time through the March play-off.

items.title: Wales beaten by 10-man Portugal as Neto scores but is sent off
items.excerpt: Wales ended their Nations League group campaign with a 3-2 defeat against 10-man Portugal in Cardiff after Chelsea's Pedro Neto was sent off.
body: Wales ended their Nations League group campaign with a 3-2 defeat against 10-man Portugal in Cardiff after Chelsea's Pedro Neto was sent off.

Although there was little riding on the contest, with Wales guaranteed a League A relegation/promotion play-off in March and Portugal having qualified for the quarter-finals, the two sides produced an entertaining spectacle.
Portugal skipper Bruno Fernandes blasted the opener after 11 minutes, but that was immediately wiped out by David Brooks' ninth goal for Wales. As it happened | Teams | Stats Nations League tables
Sorba Thomas broke free to put Wales ahead before the break, but again there was a quickfire response as Neto pounced to restore parity.
